chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hajjal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Extend your hand to me so I may kiss it.' So he extended it to me. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, your head as well.' So he did. I kissed it. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, your legs as well.' He said, 'I have sworn, I have sworn, I have sworn' three times; 'And there remains something, there remains something, there remains something.'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a phrase of deep reverence)

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette and significance of kissing the hands and head of the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Yunus ibn Yaqoub demonstrates the Shia practice of *ta'zim* (veneration) by kissing the hands, head, and feet of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who responds with repeated emphasis ('I have sworn') to validate the act. The phrase 'and there remained something' suggests the continuous, boundless honor due to the Imams, reinforcing their spiritual status as the living proofs of God. This interaction highlights the physical manifestation of reverence for the Ahl al-Bayt, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence and theology regarding the respect owed to the Prophetic family.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hajjal, from Yunus bin Yaqoub who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Give me your<sup>asws</sup> hand, so I can kiss it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> gave it to me. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Your<sup>asws</sup> (fore) head (as well)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> did. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Your<sup>asws</sup> leg (as well)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You oathed, you oathed you oathed’, three times; ‘And there remains something, there remains something, there remains something’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hajjal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“Once I went to see abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and I asked, ‘Can I kiss your hand, please?’ The Imam agreed and I kissed his hand. I then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, can I kiss your head, please?’ The Imam agreed and I kissed his head. Then I asked, ‘Can I kiss your feet, please?’ The Imam said, ‘You had vowed, you had vowed, you had vowed, three and one remains, one remains, and one remains.” (The Imam perhaps indicated that the narrator, in fact, had vowed to kiss the Imam’s (a) hand, (b) head and (c) feet).”’
